links.outcome: Hallucination rate in contrast media consultation with vs without RAG grounding in guidelines
links.effect: Hallucinations present in 8% of base Llama responses and eliminated (0%) with RAG (Yates χ²=6.38, p=0.012; Fisher p=0.0068); mean rank improved by 1.3.
links.quote: Qualitative assessment by a radiologist revealed that hallucinations—particularly in contrast dosing and contraindication recommendations—were present in 8% of responses from the base Llama model and were eliminated (0%) in the RAG-enhanced version (χ²₍Yates₎ = 6.38, p = 0.012; Fisher p = 0.0068).

links.outcome: Dosing and contraindication errors in base LLM output on contrast media scenarios
links.effect: Base Llama produced hallucinations in 8% of responses, involving incorrect contrast dosing and contraindication identification; none in the cloud models or RAG version.
links.quote: These hallucinations typically involved incorrect ICM protocols, including improper contraindication identification and dosage recommendations, which could potentially impact patient safety (Table 2 ).

links.outcome: Divergence between LLM-judge and radiologist rankings of deployed configurations
links.effect: All three LLM judges ranked RAG Llama above GPT-4o mini, whereas the radiologist ranked GPT-4o mini higher (mean rank 3.21 vs 3.54).
links.quote: All three LLM evaluators consistently ranked the RAG-enhanced Llama 3.2 11B higher than GPT-4o mini, contrary to the radiologist’s assessment (Table 1 ).
